subject.title: [Feature]: Memory indexing lacks checkpoint/resume capability for long-running operations

question: Should builtin memory-core add durable checkpoint/resume for full reindex operations, and should that be automatic behavior, a reusable shadow-DB design, or a user-visible `memorySearch` option?
rationale: The source-proven gap is real, but the fix changes durable memory state, safe-publish semantics, and possibly public configuration, so automation should not choose the product contract alone.

options.title: Sponsor automatic checkpoint/resume
options.body: Design memory-core to resume interrupted full reindexes by default while preserving the existing safe-publish invariant and adding status/tests/docs for incomplete generations.

options.title: Keep safe rebuild and improve retries/status only
options.body: Treat process-death progress loss as acceptable for now and focus narrower work on retry, metadata, and clearer operator status around failed rebuilds.

options.title: Require explicit opt-in configuration
options.body: Add checkpoint/resume behind a documented config switch with upgrade proof for both default compatibility and opt-in behavior.

recommendation.title: Sponsor automatic checkpoint/resume
recommendation.body: Design memory-core to resume interrupted full reindexes by default while preserving the existing safe-publish invariant and adding status/tests/docs for incomplete generations.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest visible history on memory-core reindex architecture and already carried the prior maintainer-facing review context for this issue.
